key_insight: Commit contiguous, longest stable prefixes (LSP) instead of scattered high‑confidence tokens to preserve KV cache locality and avoid repeated repairs, enabling much faster and more coherent DLM inference.
problem_solved: Diffusion Language Models suffer from 'scattered acceptance' that fractures the KV cache, destroys memory locality, and forces costly repeated recomputation and local repairs during decoding — this paper fixes the decoding scheduler to eliminate those inefficiencies.
method: Detect token stability across diffusion iterations and compute the longest contiguous prefix that is stable (Longest Stable Prefix, LSP).
Commit the LSP incrementally so the KV cache can be updated and reused in-place, avoiding random writes/reads that fragment memory locality.
Schedule parallel generation only on the remaining unstable suffix and perform targeted, efficient repairs when instability appears, minimizing recomputation.
impact: Faster, more memory-efficient DLM decoding with improved output coherence and reduced latency — directly beneficial for hardware accelerators and large-scale deployment of diffusion-based text models.
visual_elements: Side-by-side schematic: 'Scattered Acceptance' vs 'Longest Stable Prefix' showing token commit patterns and KV cache fragmentation vs continuity

paper_title: Beyond Scattered Acceptance: Fast and Coherent Inference for DLMs via Longest Stable Prefixes
paper_authors: Pengxiang Li, Joey Tsai, Hongwei Xue, Kunyu Shi, Shilin Yan
